concepts.title: Differential staining
concepts.quote: The Gram stain procedure is a differential staining procedure that involves multiple steps.

concepts.title: Crystal violet retention
concepts.quote: Cells that have thick peptidoglycan layers in their cell walls are much less affected by the decolorizing agent; they generally retain the crystal violet dye and remain purple.

concepts.title: Decolourisation
concepts.quote: However, the decolorizing agent more easily washes the dye out of cells with thinner peptidoglycan layers, making them again colorless.

concepts.title: Counterstaining
concepts.quote: This stains the decolorized cells pink and is less noticeable in the cells that still contain the crystal violet dye.

concepts.title: Cell-wall damage
concepts.quote: First, older bacterial cells may have damage to their cell walls that causes them to appear gram- negative even if the species is gram-positive.

concepts.title: Interpretation errors
concepts.quote: Second, errors such as leaving on decolorizer too long can affect the results.
